moments.selftext: Abraham Lincoln stood about 6’4” (193 cm), and when wearing his signature hat, he was nearly 7 feet tall. He was also reportedly very self-conscious about the unusually large size of his hands. Lincoln’s height was particularly remarkable for the mid-1800s, when the average American man stood around 5’8” (173 cm). Standing 6’4” (193 cm), Lincoln was noticeably taller than most people around him. His long arms and legs, large hands and feet, and lean, muscular build were shaped in part by years of farm work, rail splitting, and other demanding physical labor. As a young man, Lincoln was also known as a skilled wrestler. His well-known 1831 match against Jack Armstrong helped build his reputation in New Salem, Illinois. He was reportedly an exceptional competitor, with a record often cited as roughly 300 wins and only one loss.

moments.title: “Everybody wants to save the Earth; nobody wants to help Mom do the dishes.” - P.J. O'Rourke This quote points to a familiar contradiction in human behavior: people are often drawn to large, heroic causes while overlooki
moments.selftext: “Everybody wants to save the Earth; nobody wants to help Mom do the dishes.” - P.J. O'Rourke This quote points to a familiar contradiction in human behavior: people are often drawn to large, heroic causes while overlooking the smaller responsibilities directly around them. Grand missions, such as saving the planet, can feel inspiring and meaningful because they are ambitious, visible, and widely praised. Yet character and compassion are often revealed through the ordinary tasks of everyday life. Washing the dishes or helping someone at home may receive little recognition, but these simple actions require genuine effort and consideration. The quote humorously suggests that changing the world begins with taking responsibility for the small things and helping those closest to us.

moments.title: Paul Christiano, founder of the Alignment Research Center, is joining the OpenAI Foundation Board and its Safety and Security Committee, which provides governance over the safety and security practices across OpenAI. As
moments.selftext: Paul Christiano, founder of the Alignment Research Center, is joining the OpenAI Foundation Board and its Safety and Security Committee, which provides governance over the safety and security practices across OpenAI. As AI capabilities advance, strong safety, security, alignment, and governance matter more than ever. Paul’s work on AI alignment and his years at @NIST will strengthen the Foundation’s oversight, bringing an independent voice to challenge assumptions, assess safeguards, and reinforce accountability around critical decisions. Paul will also serve as a non-voting observer on the OpenAI Group PBC Board.
